messages.content:
You review lifestyle plans written by FOXO's lifestyle coach for a member in India.

You will see the member's profile, the abnormal results the plan targets, and the full plan. Judge whether a member could act on the plan tomorrow. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- specific: Recommendations give concrete foods with portions or timing, not generic advice like "eat healthy".
- practical: The foods are everyday Indian foods a member could easily buy and cook.
- explained: Each recommendation says how it helps the linked biomarker.
- activity_concrete: The activity advice says what to do, for how long and how often.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Diet: vegetarian. Allergies: tree nut. Conditions: none.
Abnormal results: haemoglobin 10.9 g/dL (low), vitamin_d 21.0 ng/mL (low)

Plan:
Focus areas: Raise low haemoglobin with iron-rich vegetarian foods and vitamin C at meals; Improve low vitamin D with fortified foods and safe morning sunlight; Keep activity gentle until haemoglobin is rechecked, as the doctor advised
Foods to eat:
- At lunch and dinner, eat 1 katori (about 150 g cooked) dal or sprouted moong/chana, with a squeeze of lemon or a small tomato salad. (why: Pulses give vegetarian iron, and lemon/tomato vitamin C helps your body absorb it better to support low haemoglobin.; linked to haemoglobin)
- Have 1 katori cooked seasonal green leafy sabzi (palak, methi or amaranth) 4–5 times a week, or 1/2 katori cooked beetroot in salad. (why: Everyday Indian greens and beetroot add iron to a vegetarian diet and support low haemoglobin; pair them with lemon.; linked to haemoglobin)
- Take 1 tablespoon roasted pumpkin seeds or sesame seeds (til) as a mid-morning snack, or 1 tablespoon sesame chutney with lunch. (why: Seeds are practical vegetarian iron sources for low haemoglobin; check labels for tree-nut cross-contamination because of your allergy.; linked to haemoglobin)
- Keep tea and coffee at least 1 hour away from meals; instead have lemon water, amla or guava as a snack. (why: Tea and coffee can reduce iron absorption, while vitamin C foods help absorption and support low haemoglobin.; linked to haemoglobin)
- Have 1 glass (200–250 ml) vitamin D-fortified milk or curd daily as a mid-morning or evening snack; if using plant milk, choose a fortified soya option and check it has no tree nut. (why: Fortified dairy or soya is a practical vegetarian vitamin D food; ask your FOXO doctor whether a supplement is needed for your low vitamin D.; linked to vitamin_d)
- Include 1 katori cooked mushrooms 3–4 times a week, for example in sabzi or soup. (why: Mushrooms can provide some vitamin D, especially sun-exposed mushrooms, and add variety while you improve low vitamin D.; linked to vitamin_d)
Foods to limit or avoid: Tree nuts and any food containing them — almond, cashew, pistachio, walnut, hazelnut, macadamia, pecan, Brazil nut, nut butters, cashew paste, nut-based sweets, gravies and bakery items; check labels strictly because of your tree-nut allergy.; Tea, coffee and cola with meals — keep at least a 1-hour gap before or after meals.; Packaged snacks, maida bakery items and sweets that may contain tree nuts — check labels before eating.; Nut-based milks, nut butters, cashew paste and nut-containing chutneys — avoid completely due to tree-nut allergy.
Activity: Follow your doctor's restriction: no heavy lifting or high-intensity exercise until haemoglobin is rechecked. Try a gentle 10–15 minute easy walk after meals, and get 10–15 minutes of safe morning sunlight 3–4 times a week if your doctor agrees. Stop if you feel dizzy, breathless or very tired, and ask your FOXO doctor before increasing activity.
Sleep: Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep with a regular bedtime; keep screens away 30–60 minutes before bed. If you feel very tired or breathless, rest and contact your FOXO doctor.
Retest in 12 weeks

response: {"criteria": [{"criterion": "specific", "reasoning": "Every food recommendation gives a concrete item with a portion (e.g., 1 katori dal, 1 tablespoon seeds, 200–250 ml fortified milk) and timing or frequency (lunch/dinner, mid-morning snack, 4–5 times a week, 1-hour gap from meals for tea/coffee).", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "practical", "reasoning": "The foods listed — dal, sprouted moong/chana, palak/methi sabzi, beetroot, sesame seeds and chutney, amla, guava, curd, mushrooms — are everyday Indian vegetarian staples that are easy to buy and cook.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "explained", "reasoning": "Each food item includes a 'why' statement explaining the mechanism (iron from pulses/greens/seeds, vitamin C aiding absorption, tea/coffee hindering absorption, fortified milk and mushrooms for vitamin D) and explicitly links it to the relevant biomarker.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "activity_concrete", "reasoning": "The activity advice specifies what to do (easy walk, morning sunlight), duration (10–15 minutes each), and frequency (walk after meals, sunlight 3–4 times a week), plus clear safety limits on intensity until haemoglobin is rechecked.", "passed": true}]}
